# lean-pkg claims

claims.yaml: sync \| list \| check \| migrate \| ledger \| mark \| rebase (named reusable results).

## Usage

```text
lean-pkg claims [common flags] [COMMAND]
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

## Subcommands

- [`lean-pkg claims sync`](#lean-pkg-claims-sync): read claims.yaml at HEAD of the checkout; validate (TODO placeholders refused); cache; event
- [`lean-pkg claims list`](#lean-pkg-claims-list): table of cached claims with status and trust
- [`lean-pkg claims check`](#lean-pkg-claims-check): re-validate cached claims; exit 0/1 (--file: a working-copy file)
- [`lean-pkg claims migrate`](#lean-pkg-claims-migrate): legacy claims.json -&gt; a claims/1 skeleton in the checkout (never the registry)
- [`lean-pkg claims ledger`](#lean-pkg-claims-ledger): per-claim closure from the recorded evidence: verified only with zero diagnostics; read-only; exit 0 only when the package is ready
- [`lean-pkg claims mark`](#lean-pkg-claims-mark): set the status of the claims a comparator config's theorem_names cover (exact full-name match); read-only unless --write; never commits
- [`lean-pkg claims rebase`](#lean-pkg-claims-rebase): move claims.yaml and coverage.yaml to a new manuscript version: carry unchanged statements re-keyed from the new .aux, list the rest for review; writes only --out-dir; never changes a status

## Exit codes

0 success (dry runs and no-ops included), 1 refused or failed, 2 usage error; see [Exit codes](../cli.md#exit-codes).

## lean-pkg claims sync

read claims.yaml at HEAD of the checkout; validate (TODO placeholders refused); cache; event.

### Usage

```text
lean-pkg claims sync [--agent AGENT] [common flags] NAME
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

### Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` |   |
| `--agent AGENT` | the agent acting (recorded as the event's actor); another agent's live lease then refuses |

### Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `claims sync NAME` | read `claims.yaml` (schema `claims/1`) at `HEAD` of the checkout, check every `decl` occurs in its `file` (a `decl` is a dotted Lean name whose components may be «quoted», as in `Demo.«foo bar»`; its last component, «» kept whole, is looked up), refuse any claim still carrying a `claims migrate` placeholder (`decl: TODO`, or a `summary` starting with `TODO`), naming the claim, cache the claims and the commit in the registry; event `claims-synced`; identical re-sync is a no-op; when the pinned commit is on no remote-tracking branch of the checkout (as of its last fetch, so never pushed) both print a stderr `WARN` naming the commit and the push to make, and `--json` carries `pin_published` (`true`, `false`, or `null` without a remote) | |

### Examples

Read claims.yaml at HEAD of the checkout, validate it and cache the claims in the registry.

```bash
lean-pkg claims sync my-proof
```

## lean-pkg claims check

re-validate cached claims; exit 0/1 (--file: a working-copy file).

### Usage

```text
lean-pkg claims check [--file PATH] [common flags] [NAME]
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

### Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` |   |
| `--file PATH` | schema-check this claims file (e.g. claims.yaml before you commit it) instead of the registry cache; schema only (no checkout, so declarations are not looked up: `claims sync` and `gate` do that); reads no registry; NAME, if given, must be its package |

### Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `claims check [NAME]` | re-validate cached claims (schema, unique ids, acyclic supersession, declarations at the synced commit); exit 0 or 1. `--file PATH` instead schema-checks a working-copy claims file (schema only: there is no checkout, so declarations are not looked up; validate `claims.yaml` before the commit you will gate): no registry is read, `NAME` is optional and, if given, must be the file's `package`; `PASS`/`FAIL` first, exit 0 or 1, `--json` `{ok, path, claims, errors[]}`. With `NAME`, coverage `none` (no cached claims, no `claims.yaml` at HEAD) or `unsynced` (`claims.yaml` committed, nothing cached) is a failure (exit 1): no coverage is not ok. `--json` adds `coverage`, `cached_claims`, `claims_yaml` (`present`, `absent`, `unknown`), `legacy_claims[]` and `hint` per package. Without `NAME`, packages with no claims are skipped as before. A `NAME` that is an existing `.yaml`, `.yml` or `.json` file is a usage error naming `--file` (exit 2) | `[--file PATH]` |

### Exit codes

Exit 1 is also a negative answer here:

- `claims check [NAME]`: invalid claims, or none synced

### JSON output

Top-level keys of `--json`, as recorded in the golden contract (tests/golden/json-keys.json):

- `claims-check` (exit 1): `ok`, `packages`, `warnings`

### Examples

Schema-check a working-copy claims.yaml without the registry.

```bash
lean-pkg claims check --file claims.yaml
```

## lean-pkg claims migrate

legacy claims.json -&gt; a claims/1 skeleton in the checkout (never the registry).

### Usage

```text

                        [common flags] NAME
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

### Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` |   |
| `--from PATH` | the legacy JSON (relative paths are read from the checkout). Required. |
| `--out OUT` | repo-relative output (default: claims_file, else claims.yaml) |
| `--dry-run` | print the skeleton; write nothing |
| `--agent AGENT` | your lease agent, when the package is leased |

### Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `claims migrate NAME --from PATH` | convert a legacy claims JSON (a list of rows, rows under `claims`/`rows`/`items`/`entries`, or a mapping id to row; `PATH` relative to the checkout) into a `claims/1` skeleton in the checkout: mapped fields are copied (`claim_id`/`id`, `lean_decl`/`decl`, `statement`/`summary`, `lean_file`/`file`, `type`/`kind`, `paper_ref`/`citation`, `tags`/`keywords`, `depends_on`), the rest get `TODO` markers (`decl: TODO`, `summary: TODO: ...`, `file: TODO.lean`, each of which `claims sync` refuses) listed in a comment header with any unmapped keys. Never overwrites, never writes the registry or the event log, and grants no verification: commit the finished file, then `claims sync` | `[--out claims.yaml]` `[--dry-run]` `[--agent A]` `[--json]` |

## lean-pkg claims ledger

per-claim closure from the recorded evidence: verified only with zero diagnostics; read-only; exit 0 only when the package is ready.

### Usage

```text
lean-pkg claims ledger [--stage {gate,promote}] [common flags] NAME
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

### Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` |   |
| `--stage {gate,promote}` | the authority required: gate (lower tier) or promote (also the comparator tier for every reusable theorem and lemma; the default). Choices: `gate`, `promote`. |

### Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `claims ledger NAME` | read-only, nothing stored: each claim (the claims file at the gate-bound commit, else the cache, else the file committed at `HEAD`) with named diagnostics from the recorded receipts, re-checked with `gate`'s and `promote`'s validators; a claim is `verified` only with zero diagnostics, else `out-of-scope`, `blocked`, `unknown` or `open`; the package is `ready`, `open`, `failed` or `unknown` (fails closed: no claims or no `reusable` claim is `unknown`); `--stage promote` (default) also requires the comparator tier for reusable theorems and lemmas, `--stage gate` only the lower tier; exit 0 only when `ready`; `--json` adds `ledger_digest`; codes and rules in [Lifecycle](../lifecycle.md#claims-ledger). Manuscript findings (`manuscript_findings`, `statement_basis: corrected`; [schema](../prior-art.md#manuscript-findings)) are listed per claim with one summary line and `--json` `manuscript_findings`, and change no status; a `lean_evidence` declaration missing at the gate-bound commit is `finding-evidence-missing` | `[--stage gate\|promote]` `[--json]` |

### Exit codes

Exit 1 is also a negative answer here:

- `claims ledger NAME`: the ledger is not ready

### JSON output

Top-level keys of `--json`, as recorded in the golden contract (tests/golden/json-keys.json):

- `claims-ledger` (exit 0): `bound_commit`, `claims`, `claims_source`, `comparator_sha256`, `counts`, `ledger_digest`, `manuscript_findings`, `name`, `ok`, `package_status`, `reasons`, `receipt_sha256`, `required`, `schema`, `stage`

## lean-pkg claims mark

set the status of the claims a comparator config's theorem_names cover (exact full-name match); read-only unless --write; never commits.

### Usage

```text
lean-pkg claims mark --from-comparator CONFIG.json
                     --status {reusable,internal,experimental} [--write] [--dry-run]
                     [--agent AGENT] [common flags] NAME
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

### Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` |   |
| `--from-comparator CONFIG.json` | the comparator configuration whose theorem_names select the claims (relative paths are read from the checkout). Required. |
| `--status {reusable,internal,experimental}` | the status to set. Required. Choices: `reusable`, `internal`, `experimental`. |
| `--write` | edit the claims file in the checkout (only the status values; never committed) |
| `--dry-run` | print the changes; write nothing (the default) |
| `--agent AGENT` | with --write: the lease holder, when the package is leased |

### Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `claims mark NAME` | set `status` on exactly the claims whose `decl` a comparator configuration's `theorem_names` cover (the `comparator config --coverage` and ledger rule: the full name, or `<Prefix>.<decl>`, of a fully qualified decl; a shared last component never matches), in the checkout's working copy of the claims file; read-only unless `--write` (the default prints the plan); `--write` edits only the changed `status:` values (comments and layout kept; when that is impossible the file is re-dumped and the output says so), validates the result against `claims/1`, never commits and never writes the registry; another agent's live lease refuses `--write`; configuration names that cover no claim are listed (`unmatched theorem name: ...`); next: commit, `claims sync`, re-gate. `claims sync` and `claims check` print `WARN NAME: gated, N claim(s), none with status reusable: ...` (JSON `warnings[]`) for a gated package with claims and none `reusable`, and the ledger's `unknown` reason names this fix. `--json` {ok, name, file, config, status, matched[] {id, decl, from, to, changed}, changed, unmatched[], written, reformatted} | `--from-comparator CONFIG.json` `--status reusable\|internal\|experimental` `[--write \| --dry-run]` `[--agent A]` `[--json]` |

## lean-pkg claims rebase

move claims.yaml and coverage.yaml to a new manuscript version: carry unchanged statements re-keyed from the new .aux, list the rest for review; writes only --out-dir; never changes a status.

### Usage

```text
lean-pkg claims rebase --from-tex OLD.tex --to-tex NEW.tex --to-aux NEW.aux
                       [--from-aux OLD.aux] [--from-sha256 HEX]
                       [--to-version arXiv:IDvN] [--to-commit HEX] [--to-repo URL]
                       [--unwrap-macro NAME] [--claims-file PATH] [--coverage-file PATH]
                       [--out-dir DIR] [common flags] NAME
```

`[common flags]`: `--json`, `--commit`, `--push`, `--no-commit`, also accepted before the command name; see the [CLI overview](../cli.md).

### Arguments and flags

| Argument or flag | Description |
|---|---|
| `NAME` |   |
| `--from-tex OLD.tex` | the (flattened) TeX the claims were written against; its SHA-256 must match coverage.yaml's manuscript sha256 (an arXiv version: a .tex of its source-baseline record), or --from-sha256 when none is recorded. Required. |
| `--to-tex NEW.tex` | the new version's (flattened) TeX. Required. |
| `--to-aux NEW.aux` | the .aux of a full build of NEW.tex: new numbers and pages come from it. Required. |
| `--from-aux OLD.aux` | the old .aux: resolves references written as numbers (Lemma 4.2, (3.7)) to TeX labels |
| `--from-sha256 HEX` | the SHA-256 of OLD.tex, required when coverage.yaml records none (checked, never trusted) |
| `--to-version arXiv:IDvN` | the new manuscript.version for the proposed coverage.yaml |
| `--to-commit HEX` | or: the manuscript repo commit of NEW.tex (sha256 is NEW.tex's) |
| `--to-repo URL` | with --to-commit: the manuscript repo (default: coverage.yaml's) |
| `--unwrap-macro NAME` | also read \\NAME{X} as X (a revision-highlight macro); repeatable |
| `--claims-file PATH` | a working-copy claims file instead of the one committed at HEAD |
| `--coverage-file PATH` | a working-copy coverage file instead of coverage.yaml committed at HEAD |
| `--out-dir DIR` | write the proposals, the report and the review packet here (a new or empty directory); without it nothing is written |

### Details

| Form | What it does | Key flags |
|---|---|---|
| `claims rebase NAME --from-tex OLD.tex --to-tex NEW.tex --to-aux NEW.aux` | move `claims.yaml` and `coverage.yaml` (committed at `HEAD`) to a new manuscript version (#6); never writes the registry or the checkout, never changes a claim status, never sets `fixed_in`. Refused (exit 1): `OLD.tex`'s SHA-256 differs from the manuscript `sha256` `coverage.yaml` records, or is none of the `.tex` hashes of the source-baseline record of its arXiv version (`formalization anchor`; none recorded: `--from-sha256` must state it; the proposal drops `manuscript.eprint_sha256`), TeX that is not UTF-8 or has unbalanced environments, a referenced label defined twice in `OLD.tex`, `NEW.tex` or `NEW.aux`. Each referenced label (coverage `paper.label`, else `paper.number` via `--from-aux`; a finding's `location.label`; a label in a `citation`) is classified by its statement or equation environment, compared after a fixed normalization: `unchanged` (carried; number, page and line re-keyed from `NEW.aux`), `changed`, `missing`, `moved-into-proof`, `not-in-old`, `unsupported`, `unnumbered`; all but `unchanged` need review and stay as they were. `--out-dir DIR` (new or empty) gets the proposed `claims.yaml` and `coverage.yaml`, `rebase-report.json` (`claims-rebase/1`) and `.md` with old/new excerpts, `review/` excerpts and diffs, and `MANIFEST.sha256`; deterministic; without it nothing is written. Exit 0 all carried, 1 review needed or refused, 2 usage; `--json` {ok, counts, labels[], rows[], findings[], citations[], needs_review[], proposed_errors[], files[], ...}. [Move to a new manuscript version](../prior-art.md#move-to-a-new-manuscript-version) | `[--from-aux OLD.aux]` `[--from-sha256 HEX]` `[--to-version arXiv:IDvN \| --to-commit HEX [--to-repo URL]]` `[--unwrap-macro NAME ...]` `[--claims-file PATH]` `[--coverage-file PATH]` `[--out-dir DIR]` `[--json]` |

### JSON output

Top-level keys of `--json`, as recorded in the golden contract (tests/golden/json-keys.json):

- `claims-rebase` (exit 0): `citations`, `counts`, `files`, `findings`, `inputs`, `labels`, `name`, `needs_review`, `normalizations`, `ok`, `out_dir`, `proposed_errors`, `rows`, `statuses_changed`, `to_version`, `warnings`, `written`
